claims.claim_text: Wallach says extreme calorie and carbohydrate restriction lowers your active thyroid hormone, because the thyroid responds to how much you eat.
claims.verbatim: Thyroid hormone: It is clear that both the caloric content and the carbohydrate content of the diet affect thyroid metabolism. The thy- roid gland functions as a thermostat for the body’s basal temperature and metabolic rate. Increases in calories and carbohydrates increase the metabolically active hormones, while extreme restriction decreases the levels of active thyroid hormone.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says mild exercise increases muscle mass and bone density well into old age.
claims.verbatim: Mild exercise increases muscle mass and bone density well into old age.

claims.claim_text: Wallach cites nutrition professor Bruce Holub that trans fats, found in hydrogenated oils, raise LDL 'bad' cholesterol and triglycerides while lowering protective HDL 'good' cholesterol.
claims.verbatim: “Besides increasing the number of LDL (bad) cholesterol and trig- lycerides in the bloodstream, trans fats also lower your HDL (good) cholesterol,” says Bruce Holub, Ph.D., a professor of nutrition at the University of Guelph, Canada. “Trans fats also increase blood levels of acompound called lipoprotein a. The more of this lipoprotein you have in your system, the greater your risk of developing heart dis- ease,” he said.

claims.claim_text: Wallach argues LDL is not a separate 'bad' cholesterol but ordinary cholesterol that has been oxidized and damaged by free radicals when it isn't protected by antioxidants.
claims.verbatim: Total cholesterol is analogous to paint on a house. All of the paint on the house came from the same paint can, yet the paint on the western exposure often times blisters, powders, oxidizes and flakes before the rest of the paint because as the sun sets in the west it produces an intense heat damage. Like wise the total circulating cho- lesterol comes from the same bucket, however, unprotected by anti- oxidants, a portion of the total will be damaged and become LDL. LDL is not a separate species of cholesterol, it is just damaged choles- terol and damaged cholesterol produces inflammation.

claims.claim_text: Wallach warns cholesterol-lowering drugs carry real risks: the statin Baycol was withdrawn after it caused a potentially fatal muscle-breakdown disease called rhabdomyolysis.
claims.verbatim: Bayer Pharmaceuticals withdrew it’s cholesterol lowering drug Baycol because the drug produced a potentially fatal muscle break- down disease called rhabdomyolysis.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says cholesterol can be brought into the normal range without drugs using a complete 90-nutrient program — especially chromium, vanadium, essential fatty acids, niacin and antioxidants like selenium, green tea and dark berries — plus a low-carbohydrate diet.
claims.verbatim: The non drug alternatives that can be used to bring cholesterol into the normal range (220 - 270), includesya complete supplement program that provides all of the known 90 essential nutrients. In particular, chromium, vanadium, essential fatty acids, niacin and antioxidants (selenium, green tea, vegetables, dark berries, etc.) and a low carbohydrate diet are all known to bring cholesterol into the normal range.

claims.claim_text: Wallach reports that pterostilbene, a cholesterol-regulating compound in blueberries, matched or beat statin drugs at lowering cholesterol in a comparative study, without their side effects.
claims.verbatim: Scientists praised a new cholesterol regulating compound in blue- berries called pterostilbene. In a comparative study with “statin” drugs, pterostilbene equaled or exceeded the cholesterol lowering proper- ties of the drugs; additionally pterostilbene does not have any nega- tive side effects.

claims.claim_text: Wallach lists brain disorders (dementia) among the signs of chromium deficiency, alongside the blood-sugar problems -- hypoglycemia, high insulin and diabetes -- that low chromium also causes.
claims.verbatim: Signs of Chromium Deficiency in the Human ¢ Impaired glucose tolerance (hypoglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, diabetes) ¢ Elevated circulating insulin ¢ Glycosuria (sugar in the urine) ¢ Fasting hyperglycemia (elevated blood sugar) ¢ Impaired growth ¢ Decreased longevity ¢ Elevated serum cholesterol and triglycerides ¢ Increased incidence of aortic plaque (arteriosclerosis) ¢ Peripheral neuropathy ¢ Brain disorders (dementia) * Decreased fertility and lowered sperm count Anderson, 1981

claims.claim_text: Wallach recounts that Vioxx, marketed as an arthritis and PMS pain killer, was withdrawn in 2004 after being linked to as many as 139,000 fatal heart attacks.
claims.verbatim: On September 30, 2004, Merck (the $22 billion per year “Pharma Giant”) “voluntarily” withdrew Vioxx, their much vaunted arthritis and PMS pain killer, from the marketplace. Between 1999 and 2004, as many as 139,000 fatal heart attacks in the United States have been attributed to Vioxx prescriptions.

claims.claim_text: Wallach warns that failing to tell good fats from bad fats - a blind spot of low-fat dieters who cut animal foods - raises the risk of several problems, including asthma.
claims.verbatim: tend to eat lots of plant based foods rather than animals foods. Un- fortunately, the devotees don’t differentiate between good fats and bad fats, which results in many health problems, including an in- creased risk of stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, seizure disorders and asthma.

claims.verbatim: Serevent, an asthma drug “that has shown with 90 percent cer- tainty in a long term trial in England, to cause death from asthma,” says Graham. “We've got case reports of people dying, clutching their Serevent inhaler,”

claims.claim_text: Wallach names antioxidant-rich foods -- berries, red grapes, pomegranate, broccoli, kale, spinach, red bell peppers and green tea -- as protection against the free radicals behind cataracts.
claims.verbatim: Antioxidants are found in substantial quantities in: Fruit - blueberries, cherries, kiwis, pink grapefruit, oranges, plums, prunes, raisins, raspberries, red grapes, strawberries, boysenberries, pomegranate, noni and mangostein. Vegetables - alfalfa, beets, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, eggplant, kale, tomatoes, red bell peppers, spinach, tomatoes. Green tea - EGCG Antioxidants are essential to a long and healthy life and they are especially important to the obese human and the obese per- son who wants to loose weight. When body fat is burned, waste products (trans fats, oxidized fats and ceroid lipofucsin) are pro- duced. These fat metabolism waste products are free radicals and they significantly increase the risk of cancer, heart disease, vascular disease (arteriosclerosis, atherosclerosis), thrombotic disease (stroke, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and coronary thrombosis), macular degeneration, cataracts and Alzheimer’s disease.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that beriberi -- a nervous-system disease of weakness, numbness and paralysis -- is caused by the loss of thiamine (vitamin B1) when the bran is polished off white rice.
claims.verbatim: In 1901, Dr. Gerrit Grijns, a Dutch doctor, has shown that Beri- beri, a disease that affects the nervous system and is characterized by weakness, numbness, and paralysis is caused by the deficiency of a nutrient (thiamine - B1) removed when white rice is polished (re- moval of the bran).

claims.claim_text: In Hell's Kitchen, Wallach cites Graham warning that Accutane -- an acne drug linked to birth defects -- represents a 20 year FDA failure and that its sales should be immediately restricted.
claims.verbatim: Accutane, an acne drug that is linked to birth defects, “repre- sents a 20 year failure by the FDA and that sales should be immedi- ately restricted,” says Graham.

claims.claim_text: Wallach notes that in America the poor are fatter than the rich because cheap, filling calories come mostly from high-carbohydrate, high-sugar foods, while wealthier, better-educated people eat more protein and take more supplements.
claims.verbatim: One of the unexpected observations that visitors to the United States report is that rich people are skinny and poor people are obese. The lower your income, the fatter you are! One out of every four of the people with below poverty incomes is obese, by contrast in house- holds earning more than $67,000 per year show an obesity rate of one out of six - minorities show an obesity rate of one out of three. Wealthy people tend to be more educated and educated people tend to eat more protein and take more supplements when com- pared with the economically stressed. If one disregards all other considerations, the “bang for the buck” when it comes to calories out of the grocery store, is carbohydrates. High carbohydrate, high sugar foods are cheap, tasty, they fill you up and they are commonly available.

claims.claim_text: Wallach documents obesity climbing in step with modernization worldwide, noting that in China's cities obesity rose from about 4 percent in the 1970s to 28 percent by 2000 as processed foods replaced traditional diets.
claims.verbatim: Africa - In many parts of Africa, obesity is diagnosed in more chil- dren than classical “malnutrition.” The country of Tunisia’s urban population has shifted to processed flour breads. Asia - In Shanghai, roads are today clogged with automobiles in- stead of the traditional bicycles. KFC opened a drive through restau- rant in Beijing in 2002. In all Chinese cities, obesity went from four percent in the 1970s to the twenty-eight percent level in the year 2000.

claims.claim_text: Wallach says the medical advice to eat less fat and more grain backfired, because the refined white flour people switched to (pasta, tortillas, hamburger buns) has essentially the same food value as white sugar.
claims.verbatim: We humans were stampeded to eat more carbohydrates and less fat - we gladly followed the medical advice and we ate more servings of grain, however, the grains we ate were primarily processed white flour such as pasta, tortillas and hamburger buns which essentially have the same food value as white sugar - the whiter the bread, the sooner you're dead!

claims.claim_text: Wallach blames childhood obesity on mineral-deficiency pica rather than on television, video games, or a lack of outdoor play, saying mineral-starved children who cannot eat dirt instead consume more soft drinks, juice, and junk food.
claims.verbatim: Dickens and Ford reported that twenty five percent of children eat dirt. We believe that mineral deficiency pica occurs in American children at a much higher rate than twenty five percent; we believe it occurs at eighty to 100 percent, however, because of the social con- straints against eating dirt, kids will instead consume more soft drinks, more juice, more French fries, more cookies, more cake, more pasta and generally more calories as a result of their mineral deficiencies. This mineral deficiency driven pica, not playing outdoors, watch- ing TV and playing video games, is the cause of obesity in kids.

claims.claim_text: Wallach explains that high-protein, low-carb diets help partly because animal protein supplies the iron and phosphorus that quiet pica cravings, and that adding a complete plant-derived mineral supplement makes the weight loss more dramatic and lasting.
claims.verbatim: The reduced pica behavior in high animal protein diets, that naturally contain iron and phosphorus can partially explain why high protein, modest fat and low carbohydrate diets work to re- duce weight. We have found that by adding the complete plant derived mineral supplement to the weight loss and weight man- agement programs, the weight loss will be more dramatic for all and will be maintained.

claims.claim_text: Wallach cites research suggesting artificially sweetened drinks may not help weight loss, because they can make it harder for the body to know when to stop eating; in studies, rats given the choice preferred the high-calorie sweet liquid.
claims.verbatim: “Artificially sweetened drinks might not help the (weight loss) diet, because they might make it harder for the body to know when to stop scarfing. Given a choice between (identically) flavored high and low calo- rie liquids, rats (preferentially) guzzle the high calorie stuff.”

claims.claim_text: Wallach stresses that for controlling weight it is not how many minerals you consume that counts, but how many you actually absorb, so supplemental minerals only help if the body can take them up.
claims.verbatim: Supplemental minerals are truly the prevention and cure of being overweight and obese. However, all minerals are not cre- ated equal - it doesn’t matter how many minerals or how much of each mineral you consume - what counts is how many miner- als and how much of each mineral you absorb!
